name: core.openwop.workflows.people-hr
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0149) — the People / HR cluster: Employee Onboarding Orchestrator, Offboarding & Access Revocation, and Leave/PTO Request Routing. Reasons with core.ai.chatCompletion; binds Microsoft 365 via core.openwop.http.openapi-call connectionRef, recommends HRIS actions provider-agnostically via core.openwop.connectors.hris-action (Workday today), and provider-agnostic ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow) via the core.openwop.connectors.ticket-* capability nodes (ADR 0186); every account/HRIS mutation and every team-facing send is gated by core.chat.approvalGate. All tenant-specific values are run parameters (replay-deterministic). Resolves on hosts shipping the http + ai + chat + integration packs; connections are configured under Access & data → Connections. Published under core.openwop.workflows.* (openwop-team key).
author: openwop

chains.label: Employee Onboarding Orchestrator
chains.description: On offer-accepted, plan the onboarding checklist and provision the new hire across IT (Microsoft 365), HRIS/payroll (Workday), and provider-agnostic task tracking (Jira/ServiceNow) in parallel — and, behind the same approval, invite the new hire into THIS workspace (feature.orgs.nodes.invite, ADR 0622 D3) — then summarize completion. Exceptions are surfaced for review.

newHireEmail.description: The new hire's email address. After approval, the workspace invitation is emailed here from the approving admin's own email connection. This workflow is set up for one new hire at a time.

orgId.description: Team (org) to invite the new hire into. Leave empty to invite them into this workspace. You need permission to manage members there.

ticketingBaseUrl.description: The tenant's ticketing instance REST base (Jira/ServiceNow). Empty ⇒ no ticket is created.

ticketProject.description: Project/queue key for the onboarding tasks.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are an HR operations coordinator. Produce a day-one onboarding checklist for {{params.newHireName}} ({{params.role}}): IT provisioning, payroll/HRIS setup, role-based training, and a manager checklist.

config.title: Approve provisioning this new hire across IT, HRIS, and ticketing

config.systemPrompt: Summarize onboarding completion across IT, payroll, and tasks; flag any exceptions that need a human.

chains.label: Offboarding & Access Revocation
chains.description: On termination, deprovision accounts (Microsoft 365), close access tickets (provider-agnostic Jira/ServiceNow), run final-pay in the HRIS (Workday), capture a knowledge handoff, then require a compliance attestation before completing. 1.1.0 (ADR 0617 D3): the chain has TWO lanes. The SCIM-leaver lane starts from the `host.users.user.deactivated` host event (bind it on the Event Bindings page to this workflow — see the pack README); the `trigger` entry node forwards the ids-only payload. The human-started lane runs from the gallery with `userId` as a parameter. A new gated step `deprovision-host` (feature.users.nodes.deactivate) disables THIS workspace's own account BEHIND the compliance attestation — never before it — via one `{truthy approved}` edge; it reads `userId` from the event payload, else the chain parameter. It requires the run's acting user to hold host:members:manage, so on an event-started (system) run it fails closed — by design: on that lane the host account was already disabled at the identity write (ADR 0621). `notify` reports the attestation OUTCOME on both legs (decision-aware, unconditional — the NOTIFY_OF_OUTCOME allow-list).

triggerEventName.description: The host event this chain ignites on. The event belongs to the INSTALLING HOST, not the pack (openwop-1, crosstalk 1892) — defaulted so an existing install keeps working.

ticketingBaseUrl.description: The tenant's ticketing instance REST base (Jira/ServiceNow). Empty ⇒ no ticket is transitioned.

accessTicketKey.description: The access-request ticket key / sys_id to close.

closeTransitionId.description: The provider transition id (Jira) or target state (ServiceNow) that marks the ticket closed.

userId.description: The departing employee's HOST account id (`user:<id>`, from Access & data → Users) for the human-started lane. Ignored when the run was started by the `host.users.user.deactivated` event, whose payload carries the id. Empty ⇒ the host-deprovision step fails typed (nothing to act on).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: Draft a knowledge-handoff summary for {{params.employeeName}}'s departure: owned systems, in-flight work, and who should inherit each.

chains.label: Leave / PTO Request Routing

workerId.description: The Workday worker id for a live time-off submit.
